evals.prompt: How do I override a mimir as admin on stagenet so I don't have to wait for node votes?
evals.expected_output: States that there is no admin mimir on develop: only active-node MsgMimir votes set mimirs (x/thorchain/handler_mimir.go). Notes the CLI help text 'admin only' is stale. Offers real options: vote from enough active nodes (operational keys need OperationalVotesMin, default 3; economic keys need a 2/3 supermajority), or use the mocknet env-var fallback for local testing.
assertions: Says no admin mimir tier exists and does not describe a set-admin-mimir command or admin key
Explains operational (OperationalVotesMin, default 3) vs economic (2/3 supermajority) thresholds
References IsOperationalMimir in x/thorchain/keeper/v1/keeper_mimir.go to determine the class
Does not claim a priority order of admin > node > constant

evals.prompt: Two of our active nodes voted HaltBTCTrading=1 yesterday. A churn happened this morning, then a third node voted HaltBTCTrading=1, but the mimir still isn't set and nodes_all only shows one vote. What happened?
evals.expected_output: Explains HaltBTCTrading is operational (contains HALT), so PurgeOperationalNodeMimirs at churn (manager_validator_current.go) deleted the first two votes. The third vote alone is below OperationalVotesMin (default 3), so ValueOfOperational returns -1 and nothing is set. Two more nodes need to re-vote 1.
assertions: Identifies HaltBTCTrading as operational via the HALT substring rule
Names PurgeOperationalNodeMimirs running at churn as the reason the earlier votes disappeared
Explains one vote is below OperationalVotesMin (default 3) so nothing is set, and the fix is re-voting
Does not invent a minVotes = len/3 rule or a GetMimirV2 function

evals.prompt: Add a new tunable MaxFooPerBlock (default 50) that the swap queue reads, and a regression test that sets it to 10 via node votes.
evals.expected_output: Adds MaxFooPerBlock to the ConstantName iota in constants/constant_values.go, default 50 in NewConstantValue() in constants/constants_v1.go, runs make go-generate for constantname_string.go, reads with k.GetConfigInt64(ctx, constants.MaxFooPerBlock), documents in docs/mimir.md. Regression suite uses tx-mimir blocks with key/value/signer for enough nodes, then a check against http://localhost:1317/thorchain/mimir asserting .MAXFOOPERBLOCK == 10.
assertions: Puts the enum entry in constants/constant_values.go and the default in constants/constants_v1.go NewConstantValue (not a constants_v3.go)
Regenerates constantname_string.go with make go-generate rather than hand-editing
Uses tx-mimir blocks and an asserts check with an upper-case key, not an 'expected:' field
Uses enough votes for an economic key (2/3 of active validators) since MaxFooPerBlock is not operational
Does not add a version gate
